title: Threshold recalibration for balanced-accuracy utility

motivation.evidence: SRDF v2 uses balanced_accuracy in utility but kept the validation_threshold at 0.85, which was calibrated for accuracy. Result: v2 rejected 242/600 triggered cases (40%) that v1 accepted. Framework-level mean delta dropped from +5.17 pp (v1) to +3.82 pp (v2), a regression of -1.35 pp.

hypothesis: Recalibrating validation_threshold from 0.85 to 0.75 will restore framework-level performance to at least v1, while preserving v2's superior conditional discrimination.

mechanical_rule.derivation: The utility formula is u = 0.5*bal_acc + 0.5 when safety=1 and efficiency=1. The natural acceptance criterion is 'better than random', i.e., bal_acc > 0.50. Substituting into the formula: u_min = 0.5*0.50 + 0.5 = 0.75. This value is derived from the formula, not chosen by the analyst.

H1.claim: v3 >= v1 at framework level (mean delta on 600 triggered cases).
H1.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on dataset-level deltas (v3 - v1), two-sided.

H2.claim: v3 > v2 at framework level (mean delta on 600 triggered cases).
H2.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank on dataset-level deltas (v3 - v2), two-sided.

H3.claim: v3 preserves v2's conditional superiority on accepted cases.
H3.test: Compare v3 vs v1 on cases where both accept.

cohort: Same as S06a (stage_198, 198 datasets, 600 triggered cases)
metric: Balanced accuracy on held-out test fold

stopping_rules.null_finding: If any hypothesis fails, it is documented as null. No re-run.

not_amended: The original NC-S06-CONFIRM protocol remains unchanged. This is a separate sub-study.
